title: Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization, a method that improves the reasoning ability of language models by iteratively optimizing the preference between competing generated Chain-of-Thought candidates. The approach outperforms baselines on several reasoning tasks, including GSM8K and ARC-Challenge, without using additional training data.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a math problem. You can use a language model to generate possible solutions, but how do you know which one is correct? Our approach, Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization, uses a simple yet powerful idea: preference optimization. We train a model to prefer correct solutions over incorrect ones, and then use this model to generate new solutions. By repeating this process, we can improve the model's reasoning ability.

This approach is based on the idea that preference optimization can be used to improve the performance of language models on reasoning tasks.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
Our approach consists of two main steps: Chain-of-Thought & Answer Generation and Preference Optimization. In the first step, we use a language model to generate possible solutions to a problem. In the second step, we train a model to prefer correct solutions over incorrect ones. We use a DPO+NLL loss function to train the model, which combines the DPO loss with a negative log-likelihood term.

This approach allows us to improve the model's reasoning ability by iteratively optimizing the preference between competing generated solutions.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluated our approach on several benchmark datasets, including GSM8K and ARC-Challenge. Our results show that Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization outperforms baselines on these datasets. For example, on GSM8K, our approach achieves an accuracy of 81.6% after four iterations, compared to 55.6% for the zero-shot model.

We also found that our approach improves performance on ARC-Challenge, achieving an accuracy of 86.7% after three iterations.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Our approach has several implications for the development of language models. First, it shows that preference optimization can be used to improve the reasoning ability of language models. Second, it demonstrates that iterative optimization can be used to improve performance on reasoning tasks. Finally, it highlights the importance of negative log-likelihood in training language models for reasoning tasks.

These findings have important implications for the development of more advanced language models that can reason and solve complex problems.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Our approach introduces several key innovations. First, we use a DPO+NLL loss function to train the model, which combines the DPO loss with a negative log-likelihood term. Second, we use an iterative optimization approach to improve performance on reasoning tasks. Finally, we demonstrate the importance of preference optimization in improving the reasoning ability of language models.

These innovations have important implications for the development of more advanced language models that can reason and solve complex problems.
